comment: Single source of truth for labels, model types, decision thresholds and pass/fail gates. Training, serving and tests must all read this file. No metric may be reported unless it is produced against a gate defined here.

split.notes: The outer train/test split is fixed BEFORE any label constant is fit, grouped by ncrb_group so a district never sits on both sides; every cross-row label constant, median and quantile is estimated from TRAIN ONLY. Within the train pool the fit/validation split is stratified (class label for classification, quantile bins of the target for regression, grouped for safety).

hidden_gem.label_definition: gem_quality = 100 * pct_rank_within_city( w*z(detail_rate) + (1-w)*z(review_star_mean) ), detail_rate = (n_detailed_positive + k*prior)/(n_reviews + k) with detailed positive = >=40 words and >=4 stars; review_star_mean = (sum of per-review stars + k*prior)/(n_reviews + k). Priors, z stats and percentile references are fitted on the TRAIN fold. k and w were chosen by 5-fold grouped cross-validation on the training fold only (k=20, w=0.3). Exposure (review volume) is NOT in the label; it is applied at serving time via gem_rule.

gem_rule.definition: is_hidden_gem = predicted gem_quality >= quality_min AND exposure_pct <= max_exposure_pct (exposure_pct = percentile of the place's review count within its city, observed not predicted)

hidden_gem.feature_note: review_count_log (votes) is allowed: the label no longer contains exposure. Duplicate / constant columns are excluded (competitor_density == area_business_count; city_* are constant for the single labelled city; review_count kept only as its log).
hidden_gem.dedupe: one row per (source, name, address) before splitting - Zomato repeats each restaurant ~4.4x with identical reviews

hidden_gem_class.label_definition: high_quality = 1 if gem_quality >= 80 (top ~20% of the city), else 0. Same features, same restaurant-level split and same label constants as hidden_gem.

gate_notes.pr_auc_min_over_prevalence: lift gate re-scaled for ~20% prevalence: the maximum possible lift is 1/0.20 = 5, so the old x6 gate (set for a 2.4% positive rate) is unreachable by definition

safety_score.definition: NOT a trained model. safety = weighted mean of the AVAILABLE components: crime = 100*(1 - national percentile of the district's NCRB crime level; violent 45%, crimes against women 35%, property 20%), police = 100*exp(-km_to_nearest_police/2), hospital = 100*exp(-km_to_nearest_hospital/3). Place -> district by point-in-polygon on data/safety/districts.geojson. Missing components are dropped and reported; with no components the score is unknown (null), never a default. See src/safety_index.py.
safety_score.why_not_regression: The previous regression target was our own formula over district crime rates. With the rates in X the model memorised the formula (R2 0.9999, meaningless); with them removed, place features carry no district-crime signal and R2 collapsed. A published reference table plus distances needs no learning.

collaboration_auth.label_definition: is_authentic = 1 if the place's fake-review fraction (from the independent text model) < 0.15. Features are metadata + review-set statistics only, so the text verdict never enters X. PROVENANCE WARNING: this label is a distillation of fake_detection, so its accuracy is bounded by that model and must be cross-checked against the hand-labelled holdout in data/holdout/.

fake_detection.label_definition: Kaggle 'fake reviews dataset.csv': CG (computer-generated) = fake = 1, OR (original) = real = 0. Genuinely independent of every feature.

solo_matching.label_definition: label_f = 0.55*clip(cos,0,1) + 0.20*interest_jaccard + 0.15*values + 0.10*same_city - 0.15*age_penalty, min-max normalised, positive at >= 0.62. WARNING: the label is a formula over features the model sees, so only an ABLATED evaluation counts as evidence of learning.

gem_quality_india.description: India-wide place quality (528 cities, Swiggy + Zomato). Label = own rating shrunk toward the (source, city) average, percentile within (source, city). The place's own rating and rating count are never features.

attractions_gem.label_source: average rating of a random held-out half of each place's reviews
attractions_gem.description: Sightseeing quality: predicts how the NEXT visitors rate a place from the other half of its reviews. Split by place name.

baselines.note: A classification gate may never sit below what a trivial predictor achieves. Regression: R^2 >= 0 beats the constant-mean predictor (r2_baseline_margin). Classification on imbalanced data gates on balanced_accuracy / macro_f1 / minority recall rather than raw accuracy, because a minority-oriented threshold always costs raw accuracy against the majority baseline. Baselines are written per task inside reports/metrics.json.
baselines.method: computed at train time from the held-out test labels

social_verification.purpose: Give users MORE VALID gem options: a review-derived hidden gem is only presented as verified when it also has a real, findable public presence on social/web platforms. Purely rule-based (never fitted), so it cannot overfit.
social_verification.candidate_rule: rank all places by hidden_gem_score; candidates are those at or above the hidden_gem decision_threshold
providers: official website HTML -> instagram/youtube/facebook/x/zomato profile links
social_verification.missing_data_rule: status 'no_data' (no key / no network) or 'unchecked' is reported as unknown and is NEVER converted into a pass or a score of 0-as-failure
social_verification.serving: verified candidates are ranked first; unverified candidates are still returned, flagged social_verified=false, so option count never shrinks silently

serving.rule: Features are looked up by place_id from data/india_places.csv + data/zomato_reviews_scored.csv. Missing required fields => HTTP-style 'insufficient_data' response; NEVER a fabricated default. Errors propagate - they are never converted into a score of 0.
